prerequisites: Average skills in analysis and design of algorithms and data structures, including implementing them in a programming language

learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has the necessary knowledge for using computers, developing software programs and applications, information processing.
The graduate has knowledge related to programming, mathematics, engineering and technology and has the skills to use them to create complex information technology systems.
The graduate has the necessary skills for computer program design and software systems analysis.
The graduate has the ability to apply general rules to specific problems and produce relevant solutions.
The graduate is able to identify complex problems and examine related issues to develop solving options and implement solutions.
The graduate is able to combine diverse information to formulate solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.

syllabus_topics: Basic graph theory definitions (graph, multigraph, directed graph/multigraph, walk, trail, path), basics on graph representations
In-deep study of possible graph representations
Connectivity and shortest path problems. Depth-first and breadth-first traversal of a graph. Connected and strongly-connected components.
Minimum-cost path in a graph. Dynamic programming approach. Bellman-Ford algorithm.
Dijkstra algorithm. A-star algorithm. Floyd-Warshall algorithm.
Dependency graphs, partial order and topological sorting. Topological sorting algorithms and strongly connected components algorithms.
Activity planning problem and algorithms.
Trees and forests. Minimum spanning trees. Kruskal and Prim algorithms.
NP-complete problems. Hamiltonian cycle, Traveling Salesman Problem.
Other hard problems: clique, vertex cover, coloring.
Eulerian cycle. Planar graphs: Euler's relation, K5 and K3,3 graphs, relations between number of edges and vertices.
Transport networks. Maximum flow. Ford-Fulkerson algorithm.
Maximum flow of minimum cost.
Matching problem
Modelling real world problems with graphs
Graph representation
Shortest path. Graph traversal
Minimum cost path, dynamic programming, Bellman-Ford algorithm
Minimum cost path, Dijkstra, A-star, Floyd-Warshall
Directed acyclic graphs; trees
Maximum flow and matching problems.
Graph representation (Lab)
Graph traversal, minimum length path, connected components (Lab)
Minimum cost paths (Lab)
Directed acyclic graphs (Lab).
Trees (Lab).
Hard (NP-complete) problems (Lab)
Finalizing assigned problems (Lab).
assessment_rules: Students must have at least 5 of 7 attendances to seminaries and 6 of 7 attendances to labs. A minimum grade of 5 (on a scale of 1 to 10) is required for both the written exam and the average of laboratory works.
